page.layout: One printed title page, one column of centred lines; a woodcut device in the centre with the imprint below it. Handwriting in the margins and around the device is not printed text and is left out.

l.i: Animantia hominum causa sunt generata, ut equus vehendi, boves arandi, canis venandi & custodiendi: Ipse autem homo ortus est ad mundum contemplandum & imitandum.
Cogitemus supera atq; cælestia: hæc nostra ut exigua & minima contemnamus.

page.notes: The device is a circular woodcut of a seated figure with the motto around its border. Manuscript annotations in ink (for example "Bibl. ... Augustana", "regularis", "observantiae") are handwriting and were omitted. The imprint line is set as printed: SIGISNAE is read as printed in the scan, and the numerals are CIↃ IↃ XCVII, which read MDXCVII. The hyphenated word "Philo-sophorum" and "tri-plicis" are split across lines as printed.
